newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends up, March contract expires.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends up, March contract expires.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed higher in volatile trade as the nearby spread swelled to a 0.40 cent premium in March before ending at a 0.35 cent premium.
The spot month went off the board at 11.32 cents per lb, up 0.27 cent from the previous close.

Traders said speculative short-covering in the now-expired March contract coupled with producer activity on both sides of the market in May accounted for the bulk of the day's estimated volume at 22,596 lots.

Early scale-up producer selling in May kept the contract under pressure, but late-session trade buying at the lows allowed the benchmark contract to climb over unchanged and settle slightly under the day's highs.

May fell just shy of its overhead target of 11.00 cents, rising to a high of 10.99 cents on the day. The contract ended up 0.08 cent to 10.97 cents, having ranged from 10.99 to 10.86 cents. The deferred months settled 0.06 to 0.02 cent firmer.

Dealers said continued scale-up selling by producers could cap any potential rally, pegging the contract's downside target at 10.75 cents. Fund selling is expected to emerge underneath that level, they said.
But from a technical perspective, today's close near the day's highs puts the market in a position to climb higher, they added.
The International Sugar Organization today lowered its world sugar output estimate to 123.34 million tonnes from 123.90 million tonnes, in 1996/97.
ISO also lowered its estimate of world sugar surplus to 2.80 million tonnes from 5.94 million tonnes.
Market sources said the estimate is in line with expectations and should not influence the market next week.
